parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the required Node ESM port, .mjs files, manual argparse-compatible parsing, canonicaljson output parity, zero external packages, and /output placement.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and later delegated a seven-lane verification workflow covering float repr, int parse, float parse, string escape, argparse, chunk count, and combined random fuzzing.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a multi-module port under /output, including pyint, pyfloat, pyrepr, pyunicode, canonicaljson, json encoder/escape, argparse parser/formatter, pytypes, pyerrors, and test10.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent placed the entry point and libraries in /output and artifact validation accepted the expected entry, but the final answer file remained empty because the process timed out.
parallel.verification: The parent matched sample cases, built a 1092-case differential harness, fixed argparse and formatter issues, and then launched broad child verification that remained unfinished when the run timed out.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The verifier workflow never synthesized child results, the final local corpus rerun ended with exit 137, and the official evaluator still failed 31 of 139 cases.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Node ESM, .mjs, manual parsing, byte-for-byte output, no external dependencies, no Python embedding, and /output requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single parent agent handled probing, implementation, harness construction, fuzzing, fixes, syntax checks, and final reporting without delegated child ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial run built a larger hierarchical implementation with modules for CLI argparse, formatting, UTF-8 encoding, canonicaljson, JSON encoding, numeric parsing, Python repr, sys stdio, and traceback behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run wrote all required files under /output, artifact validation found the expected test10.mjs and supporting libraries, and a final response described the delivered files.
serial.verification: The serial run checked documented samples, targeted argparse cases, 90 targeted differential cases, 1000 cumulative fuzz rounds, module syntax, import constraints, help, error, and traceback paths.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite normal closure and stronger final reporting, the official evaluator still failed 31 of 139 hidden samples, so some behavioral gaps remained unevidenced by the available trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had the full prompt and pursued Python argparse, canonicaljson, bytes repr, ESM modules, .mjs suffixes, and no external packages.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and pursued the same concrete behavior and packaging requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference is visible; both targeted the same obligations and both missed hidden evaluator coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned the implementation, then delegated seven independent verifier and fuzzing areas through a workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all work in one parent trajectory with workflows and task tools disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split late verification across many children; serial used a single integrated owner throughout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow brief supplied reference executable, source path, port path, harness path, no-output-modification rules, and required concrete divergences.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child interface boundary; it held all evolving implementation and verification context in the parent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced verifier handoff interfaces, but those briefs were adequate; the adverse issue was that their results did not return before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a compact set of modules for numeric parsing, float repr, bytes/string repr, canonical JSON encoding, argparse, and the test entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a larger hierarchical module tree covering similar behavior with separate CLI, codecs, parse, repr, json, sys, and canonicaljson directories.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The code structure differed, but both delivered /output/test10.mjs plus libraries and both landed at the same official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The verifier workflow stayed in progress and was killed before returning an aggregate result or synthesized findings to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and produced a final response summarizing the completed work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the delegated verifier results at closure; serial had no such join point and closed normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote the final /output implementation and told verifier children not to modify /output; no concrete file collision or overwrite is visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and revised /output directly from a single actor and artifact validation copied the final tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared verification workspace paths but not implementation ownership, so integration state was not the differentiating defect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel matched sample cases and a 1092-case harness, then attempted broader child fuzzing; the final local rerun was killed before producing a PASS line.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed targeted and fuzz verification, including 90/90 targeted cases, 1000 cumulative fuzz rounds, syntax checks, and final file layout checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached a coherent final verification report; parallel left the broad verifier workflow and final rerun unfinished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2399-second agent budget, returned code 143, and had zero retry budget remaining after an agent timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial exited with returncode zero after 1371.113 seconds and had 1026 seconds of cell budget remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel overran its budget during verification and closure; serial finished with substantial remaining budget despite the same official score.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed and both solutions failed with 108/139 samples, so there is no discordant pass/fail outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is that the parallel run spent its remaining budget on a seven-child verifier workflow that was killed before returning or synthesizing results, while the serial run kept verification in one trajectory and completed a final response. That difference affects closure and available verification evidence, but it did not change the official result in this pair.
parallel_contributors: Late seven-agent verification fan-out remained unfinished and contributed to timeout and empty final response.
serial_contributors: Single-actor verification and cleanup completed normally with final response and remaining budget.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two ports used different module layouts and independently fixed different surfaced parser and repr edge cases.
The available status only exposes aggregate 108/139 evaluator results, so the exact hidden failing behaviors cannot be attributed to one visible code defect from the pair evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative process difference, not an outcome-differential root cause
